title: Scaling policy candidate scorecard: regional variant sweeps (Aug 2026)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact scorecard of candidate scaling policies we ran across three regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) during the Aug 2026 sweep. Goal: find a policy class that balances p95 latency (<= 350ms target for hosted tier), operational cost delta (relative to current baseline), and safety (spill/drop events). These are mid-traffic synthetic + replayed traces (real traffic replayed against staging fleet).

Experiment notes (methodology):
- Each variant run for 72h per region; baseline traffic is a weekday mixed-signal profile (peaks at 7k qps for small-chat models, bursty long-context evals).
- Measurements: p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per token extrapolated to monthly, number of scale-fail/queue-overflow events, cold-start counts, autoscaler decision logs.
- All runs used same placement (gpu type V100-equivalent), same image and model shard config. Quantization/compaction held constant.

Scorecard table (human-readable):
Columns: variant | min_gpus | max_gpus | scale_up_trigger | scale_down_trigger | cooldown_s | p95_latency_ms | cost_delta_pct | spill_events | cold_starts | notes
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Variant A | 2 | 12 | queue_len > 1200 OR p95 > 400ms | cpu_util < 30% for 180s | 90 | 520 | +28% | 46 | 64 | aggressive headroom -> good at peak absorbing but high idle cost; oscillates on mid-load
Variant B | 1 | 10 | queue_len > 800 OR p95 > 375ms | cpu_util < 40% for 300s | 180 | 410 | +12% | 18 | 42 | conservative downscale -> lower cost but p95 slightly above SLA in eu-west at burst tails
Variant C | 2 | 8 | queue_len > 700 OR p95 > 350ms | cpu_util < 45% for 240s | 120 | 345 | -2% | 4 | 18 | best latency/cost balance overall; fewer cold starts due to modest max and faster up triggers
Variant D | 0 | 6 | queue_len > 500 OR p95 > 360ms | cpu_util < 50% for 90s | 60 | 380 | -10% | 12 | 28 | zero-min allows tight cost controls but risk of short spikes creating small spill events; works well for ap-southeast low baseline
Variant E | 3 | 16 | queue_len > 1500 OR p95 > 420ms | cpu_util < 25% for 240s | 240 | 560 | +45% | 2 | 102 | large max + slow downscale: virtually zero spills, very high cost and many cold starts when bursting from scale-to-zero windows
Variant F | 2 | 10 | adaptive: slope-based trigger (queue delta > 200/s) OR p95>340ms | cpu_util < 40% for 180s | 90 | 330 | +4% | 1 | 12 | adaptive slope + p95 combo reduced spill to near-zero and improved tail latency; slightly higher cost than C but better for unpredictable bursts

Interpretation and region-specific observations:
- us-west: high sustained peaks; Variant C and F performed best. F is marginally better for sudden, steep bursts we observed from Canary customers (fewer spool/spill events). Cost delta for F is +4%, which is acceptable for heavy customers.
- eu-west: bursty but smaller magnitude; Variant C met p95 target reliably and had negative cost delta due to less oscillation vs baseline. B showed p95 creep during tail bursts.
- ap-southeast: low steady traffic with occasional microbursts; Variant D (0-min) reduced base spend but resulted in audible user-facing spikes during microbursts. If we can add very short warmup capacity or predictive pre-warming, D could be cost-optimal.

Operational signals worth noting:
- cooldown tuning matters: long cooldown (>=180s) prevents oscillation but increases p95 during tail bursts. Short cooldowns cause oscillation when queue oscillates around threshold.
- min_gpus=0 is tempting for cost but increases cold-start frequency dramatically for models with >100ms init overhead.
- slope-based triggers (Variant F) handled steep deltas better than static queue thresholds; however slope triggers need smoothing to avoid noise sensitivity.

Recommendation (short):
- Primary pilot: roll out Variant C to eu-west and ap-southeast for 2 weeks in production-traffic mirror mode (no user-facing changes; just monitoring & rollback hooks).
- Secondary pilot: deploy Variant F in us-west for Canary customers (5% traffic), because bursts there are more aggressive and slope-based helps. Track cost vs. incident reduction.
- Do NOT enable Variant E (large headroom + slow downscale) as default due to high cost and poor cold-start profile. Use only for controlled enterprise tiers with strict latency SLA and cost-insensitive contracts.

Action items / next steps:
1) SRE: add per-region telemetry for slope trigger inputs, include sampling of request-size to validate slope signal quality (due 2026-08-26).
2) Infra: implement an optional pre-warm hook (API) that allows routing of predicted small warmup batches for 30s after scale-up to reduce cold-start penalty (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/512) (due 2026-09-03).
3) Product: define 'enterprise-latency' tier which can opt into Variant E with cost-aware billing + SLA change note (product review 2026-09-10).
4) Finance: run a 6-month projected cost model comparing baseline vs Variant C/F across top 10 customers (contact: Marina Chen).

Open questions / notes to self:
- How do kernel warm-up costs (for large-context models) skew cold-start impact? Need a microbench of first-10 tokens p50 vs later tokens per model.
- Slope trigger calibration: what smoothing window (median vs ema) prevents oscillation but keeps responsiveness? Experiment with 30s/60s/120s windows.
- Can we expose a per-customer 'burst-tolerance' flag to allow hybrid policies (min_gpus higher for flagged customers)?

Appendix (raw numbers snapshot - us-west, Variant C run summary):
- total_tokens_served: 1.9e10
- avg_utilization: 64%
- mean_scale_events_per_hour: 2.1
- median_queue_length_peak: 1,100
- p95_latency_ms: 345
- cost_delta_est_monthly: -1.8%
- spill_events: 2 (both short-lived, recovered <= 30s)

Slack and crossrefs:
- discussion: #infra-autoscale (Slack) thread ts: 2026-08-19 09:14, thread id: TBA
- jira: INFRA-3421 (sweep orchestration and analysis)
- confluence deck: scale-sweeps-aug-2026 (internal link above)

Quick retrospective (what surprised us):
- slope triggers (F) performed better than intuition predicted on very steep burst shapes seen in us-west; need to understand false-positive risk for noisy telemetry.
- tiny steady infra in ap-southeast makes zero-min tempting but cold start pain is underestimated in previous capacity docs.

If approved: I will prepare a short runbook for the pilot (steps for enabling, rollback commands, monitoring dashboards + thresholds) and schedule a 30-minute sync with SRE/product next week.

-- Arjun
